conventions.convention: Time starts at zero. A common real-valued process must be adapted, integrable, nonnegative almost surely at each time, and a supermartingale under every null law; its initial expectation is at most one, without requiring a deterministic initial value.
AC is assumed for the conditional-expectation convention inherited by test supermartingales.

The mixing distribution is a fixed probability measure. Each component is product-measurable with respect to the mixing sigma-algebra and the time-t sigma-algebra. Components are replaced by their positive parts before integration, and infinite mixture values are replaced by zero.
Anytime validity bounds the all-times event p_t ≤ α for every null law and α ∈ (0,1). At a possibly infinite stopping time, rejection is restricted to the event that the stopping time is finite.
The p-value transform is one when E_t ≤ 0 and min(1,1/E_t) otherwise; it uses the current process value rather than its running maximum.

Confidence sequences require adapted membership events for each fixed parameter and simultaneous coverage over all discrete times. No measurable structure on the parameter set or joint parameter measurability is required.
Test inversion retains precisely the parameters satisfying E_t^θ < 1/α; equality at the threshold excludes the parameter.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. A nonnegative test supermartingale for a family of null laws is a common real-valued process satisfying adaptedness, integrability, almost-sure nonnegativity, the supermartingale condition, and initial expectation at most one under every law in that family.
Assume AC. For a nonnegative test supermartingale E for a null family, every null law P and every α ∈ (0,1) satisfy P(sup over t ≥ 0 of E_t ≥ 1/α) ≤ α.

Assume AC. For a nonnegative test supermartingale, define p_t = 1 when E_t ≤ 0 and p_t = min(1,1/E_t) otherwise. This is an anytime-valid p-value process; under every null law, fixed-time superuniformity and P(τ < ∞, p_τ ≤ u) ≤ u hold for every u ∈ [0,1] and every possibly unbounded stopping time τ.
An adapted [0,1]-valued process p is anytime-valid for a null family if P(there exists t ≥ 0 with p_t ≤ α) ≤ α for every null law P and every α ∈ (0,1).
For α ∈ (0,1), set-valued rules C_t form a (1−α) confidence sequence when each fixed-parameter membership event belongs to the time-t sigma-algebra and P_θ(θ ∈ C_t for every t ≥ 0) ≥ 1−α for every θ.

published_dependencies.used_for: Discrete time starting at zero, nested sigma-algebras, and absence of completeness or trivial-initial-sigma-algebra requirements.
Adjacent-time conditional-expectation inequalities and the downward supermartingale convention.
Literal stopping-time event conditions and the distinction between bounded, finite, and possibly infinite stopping times.
The explicitly inherited AC hypothesis for conditional expectations and optional sampling.
The downward expectation inequality for the truncated first-crossing time in Ville's proof and for deterministic component times in the mixture proof.
Passing from finite-horizon crossing probabilities to the probability of ever crossing.
Measurability of nonnegative mixture integrals and exchange of component and sample-space integrals; both measures used here are probability measures.
Existence and almost-sure interpretation of conditional-expectation classes in the mixture supermartingale argument.
Event-integral characterization used to establish the mixture's conditional inequality.
